title: 28th Sitting of second session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened at 09:10 under the Deputy Speaker with routine business: attendance, the agenda, earlier minutes accepted, and committee membership changes. Two government bills had their first reading read, and a request to treat the Foreign Currency bill as an urgent matter was not accepted because the bill's report was already on the agenda. Members then debated committee reports on the uninhabited-islands lease bill, two appointments (Local Government Authority board and Human Rights Commission), the Addu City Council audits, the Foreign Currency Act amendments and, as the part ends, the Fisheries Act amendments. Votes on these were left for vote time, so no vote counts appear in this part. The text is readable but some titles and names are garbled. This part covers the debate on the Fisheries Act amendments, committee reports on the UK ambassador and the Information Commissioner appointments, and bills amending the Tax Administration Act, the Decentralization Act and a new surface-transport (Greater Male') bill. Opposition MDP members criticised the Decentralization and transport bills (council powers over land and Male' City Council vehicle-fee income), while government-aligned members supported them. In 16 votes, with 60 of 93 members present, 15 items passed, mostly 47-12, including the appointments and a Foreign Currency Act amendment package; one opposition amendment failed 12-47. The chair then closed the sitting, the last before the Majlis recess.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Defended the islands lease bill as a way to raise state income from cheaply leased islands, and asked critics to explain it plainly.
On the Addu audit, said the report covers Addu City Council only and rejected linking it to Male City Council's audit.
Defended the Fisheries amendments as protecting fishers and species, and said fisher debts were left unpaid under the previous government.
Supported the Information Commissioner nominee as a well-known person who had served in such roles, and criticised MDP's approach.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said concerns raised in committee on the islands bill were not reflected, and objected to giving the President power over how islands are used.
On the Addu audit, asked for a three-month deadline on Male City Council's audit and said the committee was not targeting any group.
Said criminalising dollar trading has failed elsewhere; argued government must fix supply, and suggested some taxes be payable in rufiyaa.
Backed the fisheries amendments but said large fish imports show the fisheries system has failed, and questioned whether 48-hour payment to fishers fixes the wider problem.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Presented the Addu audit report: procurement, land-swap pricing and vehicle issues, with referrals to the Anti-Corruption Commission and the Local Government Authority.
Said the committee follows set procedure, denied political motives, and said Male City Council's audit is already being looked at.
Presented the Foreign Currency report: new articles make selling or promoting dollars off the official rate an offence, with penalties.
Proposed amendments to the Foreign Currency bill setting what share of foreign earnings certain tourism businesses must convert to rufiyaa at banks each month.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said the islands lease bill lets the President lease islands and lagoons without open proposals, and urged protecting special sites for future generations.
Called the Local Government Authority nominee interviews routine, criticised the decentralisation overhaul and opposed that committee report.
On the Fisheries amendments, said they focus on fines, detention and jail for fishers while fishing is already struggling.
Said the Decentralization amendments take away land powers that councils and residents hold under the Constitution and would let the President direct island land to chosen users.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Presented the committee report: both nominees scored above the 75% threshold, the committee approved it unanimously, and he asked members to vote for it.
Presented the Decentralization Committee report on the amendments to the Decentralization Act.
Said no council or member had submitted concerns in committee and that all documents were shared with committee members before it decided.
On the transport bill, recalled past use of vehicle-fee money and questioned what Male' City Council does with about MVR 150 million a year.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Opposed the Addu audit report, saying it was being used politically ahead of the presidential election, and said he would not vote for it.
Said it was unfair to examine one council and not others, and wanted Male City Council's audit included.
Said the Foreign Currency amendments bring no benefit to citizens, and that dollars entering state companies end up on the black market.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said parts of the Foreign Currency amendments cannot be enforced, penalising people will not lower the dollar rate, and government should address its own spending.
Opposed the Information Commissioner nominee, saying he did not vote for him in committee and that the nominee is unsuitable.
Raised a point of order over remarks about how he awards marks in committee interviews; the chair accepted it as a point of order.
Proposed an amendment to the Foreign Currency bill removing a provision and reordering its lettering; it was defeated 12-47.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Called both nominees capable but said the 20-mark education criterion favoured a degree outside the post's field over a human-rights-law degree, which he called unfair.
Opposed the Decentralization amendments as not supported by his group, arguing island residents would not obstruct government projects and delays reflect government capacity.
On the transport bill, said its main effect is taking vehicle-fee income from Male' City Council and suggested it is aimed at the council before 2028.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Argued opposition members raise corruption selectively, pointing to audits of ministries and state firms under earlier governments, and urged support for the report.
Said Male' City Council receives about MVR 170 million a year while roads, harbours and licensing are handled by the government.
Cited about MVR 300,000 spent on a council residents' meeting and backed redirecting vehicle-fee money to a government company.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Argued every president has held similar powers over islands under set procedures, so the bill changes little in practice.
Supported the Tax Administration amendments, saying financial policy and enforcement need strengthening and that the Majlis can compel implementation of its laws.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Said earlier governments sold key national assets such as the airport company and water firms, and argued the amendments are needed.
Questioned the record of MDP members who criticised the bill and asked them to consider how the foreign currency problem arose.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Presented the Economic Committee report: action against illegal fishing vessels, revised licensed-species rules, and penalties for taking protected species.
Presented the Economic Committee report on the Tax Administration amendments, which let MIRA set tax owed when returns are not filed and revise audit powers and penalties.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Said opposition amendments filed on 10 August were not considered at committee stage, and put that on the record.
Seconded Meekail Ahmed Nasym's amendment to the Foreign Currency bill.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Seconded Mohamed Mamdooh's second and third amendments to the Foreign Currency bill.

speakers.name: Fathimath Sauda
positions: Presented the committee report: two nominees scored 92% and 86% after interviews and were judged qualified for the Human Rights Commission.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Presented the Foreign Relations Committee report recommending Jameela Ali Khalid as UK ambassador, passed by consensus of committee members present.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Presented the Independent Institutions Committee report recommending Abdul Aziz Jamal Aboobakuru as Information Commissioner, describing him as honest and capable.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Criticised ministries for sending amendments in repeated rounds, leaving committees to rush bills late at night, and raised concern over the bill's heavy fines.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Presented the National Development and Heritage Committee report on the surface-transport bill, covering Greater Male' rules, accident compensation and a demerit-point system.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Said the committee sought views from 15 institutions but discussed only the Attorney General's, and that a new Chapter 8 appeared late; asked that the bill be sent back.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Seconded Mohamed Mamdooh's fourth amendment to the Foreign Currency bill.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 22 to 24 were accepted by the chair after no amendments were submitted.
Committee membership changes for four committees were announced.
The urgent matter from the Kendhoo member was not accepted because the Foreign Currency bill's committee report was already on the agenda.
First readings were read for the bill on money obtained through crime and the Criminal Procedure Act amendment.
Debate on the Local Government Authority and Human Rights Commission appointment reports and the Addu audit report closed, with votes set for vote time.
After debate on the islands lease bill and the Foreign Currency amendments, the chair moved each bill to its third reading.
A recess ran from 10:32 to 11:03 during the Foreign Currency debate.
Bill on leasing uninhabited islands and reefs (whole-House committee decision) passed 47-12.
Mohamed Arif approved as a member of the Local Government Authority board (59-0).
Aishath Arif approved as a woman member of the Local Government Authority board with gender-equality experience (48-9).
H. Meenaz Shamaoon Hameed approved as a Human Rights Commission member (57-0).
Finance Committee report on Addu City Council audit reports (2012, 2015 to 2024) passed 47-12.
Meekail Ahmed Nasym's amendment to the Foreign Currency bill rejected 12-47.
Mohamed Mamdooh's three amendments to the Foreign Currency bill passed (47-12, 45-12, 47-12).
Foreign Currency Act (2024/32) amendment bill passed as amended, 47-12.
Fisheries Act (2019/14) amendment bill passed 59-0.
Whitediamond Jameela Ali Khalid approved as Ambassador to the United Kingdom (59-0).
Abdul Aziz Jamal Aboobakuru approved as Information Commissioner (47-11).
Tax Administration Act (2010/3) amendment bill passed 47-12.
Decentralization Act (2010/7) amendment bill passed 47-12.
Surface transport (Greater Male') bill passed 47-12.
The chair closed the sitting, the last before the Majlis went on recess.
